research_mode: official ONS and Home Office sources only; current YE March 2026 crime and outcomes measurements with explicit survey, recording, cohort-maturity and transition limitations; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: ONS YE March 2026 release calendar
verified_claims: the bulletin was released on 23 July 2026
the next scheduled release is 22 October 2026
limitations: release dates are publication dates, not observation dates

sources.name: CSEW headline crime 9.6 million
verified_claims: CSEW headline crime was estimated at 9.6 million incidents
there was no statistically significant change from about 9.4 million
limitations: headline crime combines several offence groups and is a survey estimate

sources.name: CSEW theft 2.6 million
verified_claims: CSEW theft was estimated at 2.6 million incidents
the change from 2.8 million was not statistically significant
limitations: survey uncertainty applies and the estimate is not a police count

sources.name: Other household theft increase
verified_claims: the rise reflected theft from outside a dwelling
limitations: the category is broader than burglary and should not be treated as parcel-level risk

sources.name: CSEW fraud 4.5 million
verified_claims: CSEW fraud was estimated at 4.5 million incidents
the change from 4.2 million was not statistically significant
limitations: recorded fraud data were not supplied for this bulletin

sources.name: Fraud victim prevalence increase
verified_claims: the number of fraud victims increased by 10%
the estimate rose to 3.8 million victims from 3.4 million
limitations: victim count and incident count are different measures

sources.name: Sexual victimisation prevalence
verified_claims: 2.1% of people aged 16 or over experienced sexual victimisation including attempts
limitations: new survey questions mean the estimate is not comparable with previous measures

sources.name: Sexual victimisation by sex
limitations: these are prevalence estimates from a redesigned self-completion module

sources.name: Harassment prevalence
verified_claims: 10.0% of people aged 16 or over experienced harassment
limitations: the measure includes one-off incidents and is broader than the police definition

sources.name: Harassment type split
limitations: categories can overlap and should not be summed without methodology checks

sources.name: Repeated harassment
limitations: repeated harassment is closer to the police course-of-conduct definition but is still survey-based

sources.name: ASB prevalence and questionnaire effect
verified_claims: question changes from April 2025 inflated part of the increase
limitations: the observed change cannot be interpreted as wholly genuine

sources.name: Homicide count
verified_claims: it was the lowest count since current recording practices began in 2003
limitations: police recorded homicide differs from the Home Office Homicide Index

sources.name: Knife-enabled crime count
verified_claims: knife-enabled crime fell by 8% to 48,774 offences
limitations: the measure uses a special collection and is not a parcel-level count

sources.name: Firearms offence count
limitations: the series excludes conventional air weapons and British Transport Police
